claim_summaries: Pointwise MH acceptance for a rational-complex microscopic basis law is an exact rational computable in polynomial bit length; the global partition cancels, but completion-conditioned proposals would introduce an unavailable partition ratio.

A k-bit downward-rounded acceptance coin gives a fixed worst-case implementation whose T-step output is within T*2^-k TV of the ideal chain; exact non-dyadic Bernoulli sampling from fair bits has no finite worst-case bound.

Coordinate-dominated refresh uses epsilon=2^-K with K=O(M+r log r+r*ell+log(1/eta)); its numeric value may be exponentially small while its binary description is polynomial. Approximate perfect-matching refresh can be sampled in fixed bit cost.
The inherited four-site example has a two-replica determinant-weight ratio and symmetric-MH acceptance exactly 2^-4L, so polynomial acceptance bit length gives no polynomial mixing guarantee.
